entries.greek: ἄν τε μακαρίσαι τινὰ θελήσῃς ... αʹ, λαʹ, μʹ, ριαʹ, ριηʹ, ρκζʹ
entries.evidence: Greek list agrees in both witnesses; each Eng psalm opens with or turns on 'Blessed is...'

entries.situation: Rebuking the plot of the Jewish leaders against the Saviour
entries.greek: μέμψασθαι τὴν Ἰουδαίων κατὰ τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἐπιβουλήν, ἔχεις τὴν δευτέραν ᾠδήν
entries.evidence: Greek ordinal δευτέραν; Ps 2:1-2 'the rulers take counsel against the LORD and His Anointed'

entries.situation: Being hounded by your own people, with many rising up against you
entries.greek: ἂν δὲ διώκῃ παρὰ τῶν ἰδίων, καὶ πολλοὺς ἔχῃς τοὺς ἐπαναστάντας ... τὸν γʹ
entries.evidence: γʹ in both witnesses; Eng 3:1 'How many rise up against me', and the superscription names Absalom, David's own son

entries.situation: Having called on the Lord in distress and been heard, and now wanting to give thanks
entries.greek: θλιβόμενος ἐπεκαλέσω τὸν Κύριον, καὶ εἰσακουσθεὶς ... τὸν τέταρτον, καὶ οδʹ, καὶ ριδʹ
entries.evidence: τέταρτον, οδʹ, ριδʹ. LXX 114 is only the first nine verses of Eng 116 (whose v.1 is 'He has heard my voice')

entries.situation: Seeing wicked people waiting to trap you and wanting God to hear your prayer; rise early and pray
entries.greek: τοὺς πονηρευομένους βλέπων ἐνεδρεύειν θέλοντας ... ὀρθρίζων τὸ πρωῒ ψάλλε τὸν εʹ
entries.evidence: εʹ in both witnesses; Eng 5:1-3 'give ear... in the morning You hear my voice'

entries.situation: Sensing the Lord's displeasure against you and being shaken by it
entries.greek: αἰσθόμενος δὲ ἀπειλῆς τοῦ Κυρίου ... ταραττόμενον ... τὸν ϛʹ καὶ τὸν λζʹ
entries.evidence: ϛʹ and λζʹ; Migne Latin '6 et 37'. Both Eng psalms open 'O LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger'

entries.situation: People scheming against you (as Ahithophel did against David) and someone telling you of it; trust God who rescues
entries.greek: βουλεύωνταί τινες κατὰ σοῦ, ὡς ὁ Ἀχιτόφελ κατὰ τοῦ Δαβίδ ... ψάλλε τὸν ζʹ
entries.evidence: ζʹ in both witnesses; Latin 'psalle 7'. The link runs through the LXX title, which names 'Chousi' (Hushai, who foiled Ahithophel). BSB reads 'Cush, a Benjamite'

entries.situation: Seeing the Saviour's grace spread everywhere and the human race saved, and wanting to address the Lord
entries.greek: βλέπων δὲ τὴν πανταχοῦ χάριν τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἐκτεταμένην ... ψάλλε τὸν ηʹ
entries.evidence: ηʹ in both witnesses; Eng 8:1 'how majestic is Your name in all the earth'

entries.situation: Singing a winepress (grape-harvest) song in thanks to the Lord
entries.greek: ᾆσαι θέλεις ἐπιλήνιον ... τὸν ηʹ καὶ τὸν πγʹ
entries.evidence: πγʹ in TLG and Migne ('τὸν η΄ χαὶ τὸν πγ΄'; Latin '8 et 83'). Both psalms carry the LXX title 'for the winepresses'; BSB 'According to Gittith' on 8 and 84. The English copy's 19 is wrong

entries.situation: When the enemy is overthrown and creation saved: not boasting in yourself but crediting the Son of God
entries.greek: ἐπὶ δὲ τῷ κατηργῆσθαι τὸν ἐχθρὸν ... λέγε τὸν εἰς αὐτὸν εἰρημένον θʹ ψαλμόν
entries.evidence: θʹ; LXX 9 is Eng 9 and 10 together. The copy's 9 is right but incomplete

entries.situation: Someone trying hard to unsettle or frighten you; hold on to your trust in the Lord
entries.greek: ἐὰν λίαν σέ τις ταράσσειν ἐθέλῃ, ἔχε σὺ τὴν πεποίθησιν εἰς τὸν Κύριον ... τὸν ιʹ
entries.evidence: ιʹ in both witnesses; Eng 11:1 'In the LORD I take refuge; how can you say to my soul, Flee...'

entries.situation: Seeing widespread arrogance and evil overflowing until nothing holy seems left among people; take refuge in the Lord
entries.greek: τὴν τῶν πολλῶν ὑπερηφανίαν ἴδῃς ... κατάφυγε σὺ ἐπὶ τὸν Κύριον, καὶ λέγε τὸν ιαʹ
entries.evidence: ιαʹ in both witnesses; Eng 12:1 'the godly are no more'

entries.situation: Opposition that drags on and on, tempting you to lose heart as though God had forgotten you; keep calling on Him
entries.greek: ἐγχρονιζούσης δὲ τῆς παρὰ τῶν ἐχθρῶν ἐπιβουλῆς, μὴ ὀλιγώρει ὡς ἐπιλησθεὶς ... ᾄδων τὸν ιβʹ
entries.evidence: ιβʹ in TLG and the Migne Greek; the Latin says 'duodecimum'. Eng 13:1 'How long, O LORD? Will You forget me forever?' The English copy's 27 is an error

entries.situation: Hearing people speak against God's providence; do not join them, but pray
entries.greek: βλασφημούντων τινῶν κατὰ τῆς Προνοίας ἀκούσῃς ... λέγε τὸν ιγʹ καὶ νβʹ
entries.evidence: ιγʹ, νβʹ; both Eng psalms open 'The fool says in his heart, There is no God'

entries.situation: Wanting to learn what kind of person is a citizen of the kingdom of heaven
entries.greek: ὁποῖός ἐστι τῆς βασιλείας τῶν οὐρανῶν ὁ πολίτης, ψάλλε τὸν ιδʹ
entries.evidence: ιδʹ; Latin '14'. Eng 15:1 'LORD, who may dwell in Your tent?'

entries.situation: Needing to pray because of people who oppose you and hem your soul in
entries.greek: προσευχῆς σοι χρεία διὰ τοὺς ἀνθεστηκότας σοι καὶ περιέχοντάς σου τὴν ψυχήν ... ιϛʹ, πεʹ, πζʹ, ρμʹ
entries.evidence: The Migne Greek reads πζ' and the Latin '16, 85, 87 et 140'. The TLG text reads πϛ (86 = Eng 87, a Zion psalm that does not fit); I followed Migne. ρμʹ in all witnesses = Eng 141, so the English copy's 140 is wrong

entries.situation: Wanting to learn how Moses prayed
entries.greek: θέλεις μαθεῖν, πῶς Μωϋσῆς προσηύξατο, ἔχεις τὸν πθʹ
entries.evidence: πθʹ; Eng 90 superscription 'A prayer of Moses, the man of God'

entries.situation: Having been saved from your enemies and rescued from those hunting you
entries.greek: ἐσώθης ἀπὸ τῶν ἐχθρῶν σου, καὶ ἐῤῥύσθης ἀπὸ τῶν διωκόντων σε ... τὸν ιζʹ ψαλμόν
entries.evidence: The Migne Greek reads ιζ’ and the Latin 'decimum septimum'. The TLG/DCO text reads ιϛ (16), which I treat as a stigma/zeta confusion. Eng 18 superscription: the day the LORD delivered him from all his enemies and from Saul

entries.situation: Marvelling at the order of creation, God's providence in it, and the holy commands of His law
entries.greek: θαυμάζεις τὴν τῆς κτίσεως τάξιν ... τοῦ τε νόμου τὰ ἱερὰ προστάγματα, ψάλλε τὸν ιηʹ καὶ τὸν κγʹ
entries.evidence: ιηʹ, κγʹ; Eng 19 is the heavens plus the law, and Eng 24 is 'The earth is the LORD's'

entries.situation: Seeing others in distress and comforting them by praying over them
entries.greek: θλιβομένους δὲ ὁρῶν, παρακάλει τούτους ... τὰ ἐν τῷ ιθʹ ψαλμῷ ῥήματα
entries.evidence: ιθʹ; Latin 'decimi noni'. Eng 20:1 'May the LORD answer you in the day of distress'

entries.situation: Seeing yourself shepherded and guided on your way by the Lord, and rejoicing in it
entries.greek: ὁρᾷς σεαυτὸν ποιμαινόμενον καὶ εὐοδούμενον παρὰ τοῦ Κυρίου ... τὸν κβʹ
entries.evidence: κβʹ; Latin '22'. Eng 23 'The LORD is my shepherd'

entries.situation: Enemies all around you; lift your soul up to God
entries.greek: οἱ ἐχθροὶ περὶ σέ, ἀλλὰ σὺ τὴν ψυχὴν ἐπαίρων πρὸς Θεόν, λέγε τὸν κδʹ
entries.evidence: κδʹ; Latin '24'. Eng 25:1 'To You, O LORD, I lift up my soul'

entries.situation: Enemies who keep on, hands full of blood, trying to drag you down and ruin you; do not leave the verdict to people, ask God to judge
entries.greek: μὴ δῷς ἀνθρώπῳ τὸ κρῖμα ... τὸν Θεὸν ἀξιῶν κριτὴν γενέσθαι ... κεʹ, λδʹ, μβʹ
entries.evidence: κεʹ, λδʹ, μβʹ; Latin '25, 34, 42'. All three Eng psalms open with a plea for God to vindicate or judge

entries.situation: The attack growing fiercer, the enemy massing like an army and scorning you as not yet anointed; do not cower
entries.greek: πλῆθος ὡς παρεμβολαὶ γένωνται ... ὡς μήπω σου χρισθέντος ... μὴ πτήξῃς, ἀλλ' ᾆδε τὸν κϛʹ
entries.evidence: κϛʹ; LXX title 'before he was anointed'; Eng 27:3 'Though an army encamps around me, my heart will not fear'

entries.situation: Schemers who are shameless: because human nature is weak, do not fix your attention on them but cry out to God
entries.greek: ἀσθενής ἐστιν ἡ φύσις τῶν ἀνθρώπων ... κράζε πρὸς τὸν Θεόν, λέγων τὰ ἐν τῷ κζʹ
entries.evidence: κζʹ; Eng 28:1 'To You, O LORD, I call'

entries.situation: Wanting to learn, with spiritual understanding, how to bring your thanks to the Lord
entries.greek: εὐχαριστῶν μαθεῖν πῶς δεῖ προσφέρειν τῷ Κυρίῳ, νοητῶς νοῶν ψάλλε τὸν κηʹ
entries.evidence: κηʹ; LXX 28:1 'Bring to the Lord' (Ἐνέγκατε τῷ κυρίῳ)

entries.situation: Dedicating your home, meaning both your soul that receives the Lord and the house you live in; give thanks
entries.greek: ἐγκαινίζων τὸν οἶκόν σου ... τόν τε κθʹ καὶ τὸν ἐν τοῖς ἀναβαθμοῖς ρκϛʹ
entries.csmv: 30 and 127 (with a bracket calling the Gradual Psalms 119-133)
entries.evidence: κθʹ, ρκϛʹ. Eng 30 superscription: song for the dedication of the house/temple. Eng 127:1 'Unless the LORD builds the house'

entries.situation: Hated and hunted by all your friends and relatives for holding to the truth, with acquaintances turning away; step back and look to what is coming
entries.greek: σαυτὸν διὰ τὴν ἀλήθειαν μισούμενον καὶ διωκόμενον παρὰ πάντων τῶν τε φίλων καὶ συγγενῶν ... τὸν λʹ
entries.evidence: λʹ; Eng 31:11 'a dread to my acquaintances; those who see me flee'

entries.situation: Seeing people baptized and redeemed, and wondering at God's love for people
entries.greek: τοὺς βαπτιζομένους καὶ λυτρουμένους ... ᾆδε εἰς ἐκείνους τὸν λαʹ
entries.evidence: λαʹ; Eng 32:1 'Blessed is he whose transgressions are forgiven'

entries.situation: Wanting to sing together with a gathering of upright people
entries.greek: ψάλλειν μετὰ πολλῶν ... τοὺς δικαίους ἄνδρας ... τὸν λβʹ
entries.evidence: λβʹ; Eng 33:1 'Sing joyfully to the LORD, O righteous ones; praise from the upright is fitting'

entries.situation: Having fallen among enemies but slipped away wisely from their scheme, and wanting to give thanks among gentle people
entries.greek: ἐμπεσὼν δὲ εἰς τοὺς ἐχθροὺς, καὶ σοφῶς αὐτοὺς διαφυγών ... τοὺς πραεῖς ἄνδρας ... τὸν λγʹ
entries.evidence: λγʹ; Eng 34 superscription: David feigning madness before Abimelech, driven away; 34:2 'the humble will hear and rejoice'

entries.situation: Seeing how eager lawbreakers are for evil, without concluding (as heretics say) that evil is in their nature: they are the cause of their own sin
entries.greek: μὴ νόμιζε ἐν αὐτοῖς κατὰ φύσιν τὴν κακίαν εἶναι, οἷα λέγουσιν οἱ αἱρετικοί ... τὸν λεʹ
entries.evidence: λεʹ; Eng 36:1-4 describes the wicked man's own plotting

entries.situation: Seeing the wicked do much wrong and lord it over the lowly, and warning yourself and others not to envy them, since they soon fade
entries.greek: μὴ προσέχειν τούτοις, μηδὲ παραζηλοῦν αὐτούς ... λέγε καὶ σαυτῷ καὶ τοῖς ἑτέροις τὸν λϛʹ
entries.evidence: λϛʹ; Eng 37:1-2 'Do not fret... do not envy... they will soon wither'

entries.situation: Having resolved to keep watch over yourself, then finding the enemy attacking all the harder, and wanting to steel yourself
entries.greek: προθέμενος προσέχειν σαυτῷ ... θέλῃς ἐπαλείφειν σαυτὸν κατ' αὐτοῦ, ᾆδε τὸν ληʹ
entries.evidence: ληʹ; Latin 'trigesimum octavum'; Eng 39:1 'I will watch my ways'

entries.situation: Enduring hardship while under attack and wanting to learn what patience gains
entries.greek: ὑπομένῃς τὰς θλίψεις, καὶ θέλῃς μαθεῖν τὴν ἐκ τῆς ὑπομονῆς ὠφέλειαν ... τὸν λθʹ
entries.evidence: λθʹ; Eng 40:1 'I waited patiently for the LORD'

entries.situation: Seeing many poor people and wanting them shown mercy: commend those who have helped and urge others to help
entries.greek: βλέπων δὲ πολλοὺς πένητας καὶ πτωχούς ... ἐν τῷ λέγειν τὸν μʹ
entries.evidence: μʹ; Latin 'quadragesimum'; Eng 41:1 'Blessed is he who cares for the poor'

entries.situation: Longing intensely for God while enemies taunt you; comfort your own soul with hope and soothe life's griefs
entries.greek: πάνυ τὸν πόθον ἔχων εἰς τὸν Θεόν ... παρακάλει σαυτοῦ τὴν ψυχὴν τῇ εἰς Θεὸν ἐλπίδι ... τὸν μαʹ
entries.evidence: μαʹ; Eng 42:1-3,10 thirst for God, 'Where is your God?' taunts, 'Hope in God'

entries.situation: Wanting to keep recalling God's kindness to the forefathers in the Exodus and the wilderness: God good, people ungrateful
entries.greek: ἀναμιμνήσκεσθαι θέλων τὰς εὐεργεσίας τοῦ Θεοῦ ... μγʹ, οζʹ, πηʹ, ρδʹ, ρεʹ, ρϛʹ, ριγʹ
entries.evidence: Greek list agrees in both witnesses; LXX 113 = Eng 114+115

entries.situation: Having fled to God and been saved from the troubles around you, and wanting to thank Him and tell how kind He was to you
entries.greek: καταφυγὼν δὲ πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν καὶ διασωθεὶς ... ἔχεις τὸν μεʹ
entries.evidence: μεʹ; Eng 46:1 'God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble'

entries.situation: You have sinned, you are ashamed and repenting, and you are asking for mercy
entries.greek: ἀλλ' ἥμαρτες, καὶ ἐντραπεὶς μεταγινώσκεις καὶ ἐλεηθῆναι ἀξιοῖς ... ἐν τῷ νʹ
entries.evidence: νʹ; Latin 'quinquagesimum'; Eng 51 superscription Nathan/Bathsheba

entries.situation: Having been slandered to a wicked ruler and seeing the devil gloat over it; withdraw
entries.greek: διεβλήθης πονηρῷ βασιλεῖ, καὶ ὁρᾷς τὸν διάβολον κατακαυχώμενον ... τὰ ἐν τῷ ναʹ
entries.evidence: ναʹ; Eng 52 superscription: Doeg informing Saul; 52:1 'Why do you boast of evil'

entries.situation: Being hunted and informed on by people who want to hand you over (as the Ziphites and Philistines did to David); do not lose heart
entries.greek: ὡς οἱ Ζιφαῖοι καὶ οἱ ἀλλόφυλοι τὸν Δαβίδ, μὴ ἀκηδιάσῃς ... τὰ ἐν τῷ νγʹ καὶ νεʹ
entries.evidence: TLG νγ, νε; Latin '53 et 55' (the Migne Greek OCR misreads 'να'). Eng 54 superscription: Ziphites; Eng 56: the Philistines seized him in Gath

entries.situation: The pursuer coming, unknowing, into the very cave where you hide; still do not cower
entries.greek: εἰσέλθῃ εἰς τὸ σπήλαιον ἐν ᾧ καὶ σὺ κρύπτῃ ... τοὺς ἐν τῷ νϛʹ καὶ τοὺς ἐν τῷ ρμαʹ
entries.evidence: νϛʹ, ρμαʹ; Latin '56 et 141'; both Eng superscriptions: 'in the cave'

entries.situation: The one plotting against you has your house watched, yet you get away; give thanks and keep it as a memorial
entries.greek: φυλαχθῆναι τὴν οἰκίαν κελεύσῃ ὁ ἐπιβουλεύων, καὶ διαφύγῃς ... τὰ ἐν τῷ νηʹ ψαλμῷ
entries.evidence: νηʹ; Eng 59 superscription: Saul sent men to watch David's house

entries.situation: Enemies insult you and people you thought were friends gossip and slander, and you are grieved for a while in your complaint
entries.greek: φλυαροῦντες διαβάλλωσιν οἱ δοκοῦντες εἶναι φίλοι, καὶ λυπηθῇς ... τὰ ἐν τῷ νδʹ ῥήματα
entries.evidence: νδʹ; Latin '54'; Eng 55:12-14 'it is not an enemy who taunts me... but you, my companion'

entries.situation: Facing hypocrites who put on a show; say this psalm to shame them
entries.greek: πρὸς μὲν ὑποκρινομένους καὶ ἐν προσώπῳ καυχωμένους ... τὸν νζʹ
entries.evidence: νζʹ; Eng 58:1 'Do you rulers indeed speak justly?'

entries.situation: People raging at you and out for your life; the fiercer they get, the more you submit to the Lord and take courage
entries.greek: πρὸς δὲ τοὺς ὁρμῶντας ἀγρίως κατὰ σοῦ ... ὑποτάσσου σὺ τῷ Κυρίῳ ... τὰ ἐν τῷ ξαʹ
entries.evidence: ξαʹ; Latin '61'; LXX 61:2 'Shall not my soul be subject (ὑποταγήσεται) to God'

entries.situation: Driven into a lonely wilderness by persecution; you are not alone there, so seek God at daybreak
entries.greek: διωκόμενος εἰς ἐρημίαν ἀπέλθῃς, μὴ φοβηθῇς ὡς μόνος ὤν ... ὀρθρίζων ψάλλε τὸν ξβʹ
entries.evidence: ξβʹ; Latin '62'; Eng 63 superscription: in the Wilderness of Judah; LXX 62:1 'I rise early to You'

entries.situation: Enemies who keep terrifying you, lying in wait and searching out everything against you, however many; do not give in, their blows are children's arrows
entries.greek: ἐκφοβούντων δὲ τῶν ἐχθρῶν ... βέλη γὰρ νηπίων ἔσονται ... τὸν ξγʹ, καὶ τὸν ξδʹ, καὶ ξθʹ, καὶ οʹ
entries.evidence: Greek list agrees in both witnesses; Latin '63, 64, 69, 70'; LXX 63:8 'the arrows of infants became their wounds' (Eng 64:7)

entries.situation: Wanting to sing a hymn to the Lord
entries.greek: ὅταν μὲν ὑμνῆσαι βούλῃ τὸν Κύριον, ᾆδε τὰ ἐν τῷ ξδʹ
entries.evidence: ξδʹ; LXX 64:2 'A hymn befits You, O God'

entries.situation: Wanting to teach someone about the resurrection
entries.greek: κατηχῆσαι θέλῃς τινὰς περὶ ἀναστάσεως, ᾆδε τὰ ἐν τῷ ξεʹ
entries.evidence: ξεʹ; LXX title 'a song of a psalm of resurrection'; Latin '65'

entries.situation: Asking God for mercy, and praising Him as you ask
entries.greek: οἰκτιρμοὺς δὲ αἰτῶν παρὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ, ὕμνει αὐτόν, ψάλλων τὸν ξϛʹ
entries.evidence: ξϛʹ; Latin '66'; Eng 67:1 'May God be gracious to us and bless us'

entries.situation: Seeing the wicked live in peace and plenty while the righteous suffer, so that you are not scandalised or shaken
entries.greek: τοὺς μὲν ἀσεβεῖς ἐν εἰρήνῃ εὐθηνουμένους ... τοὺς δὲ δικαίους θλιβομένους ... τὰ ἐν τῷ οβʹ
entries.evidence: TLG οβ; Latin '72'. Eng 73:3 'I envied the arrogant when I saw the prosperity of the wicked'

entries.situation: When God is angry with His people; words of wise consolation about it
entries.greek: ὅταν μὲν ὀργισθῇ ὁ Θεὸς ἐπὶ τὸν λαόν ... τοὺς ἐν τῷ ογʹ
entries.evidence: ογʹ; Eng 74:1 'Why does Your anger smolder against the sheep of Your pasture?'

entries.situation: When you need to give thanks to God and acknowledge Him openly (exomologesis; not confession of sin here)
entries.greek: ὅτε δὲ χρεία σοι ἐξομολογήσεώς ἐστι ψάλλε τὸν θʹ, οδʹ καὶ ϙαʹ, καὶ ρδʹ, καὶ ρεʹ, καὶ ρϛʹ, καὶ ρζʹ, καὶ ριʹ, καὶ ριζʹ, καὶ ρλεʹ, καὶ ρλζʹ
entries.evidence: TLG and the Migne Greek agree (the Migne OCR has 'οζ' for ρζ, a common ρ/ο misread). The English copy adds 71 and 126, which are not in the Greek. Each Eng psalm uses 'give thanks' language

entries.situation: Wanting to shame pagans and heretics by showing that true knowledge of God is found only in the Catholic Church
entries.greek: δυσωπῆσαι μὲν θέλων τὰ τῶν Ἑλλήνων καὶ τὰ τῶν αἱρετικῶν ... τὰ ἐν τῷ οεʹ
entries.evidence: οεʹ; Eng 76:1 'God is known in Judah'

entries.situation: Enemies have cut off your escape and you are badly pressed and shaken; do not despair, pray, and when your cry is heard, give thanks
entries.greek: τῶν δὲ ἐχθρῶν προκαταλαβόντων τὰς διεκφυγάς ... μὴ ἀπελπίσῃς, ἀλλὰ εὔχου ... τὰ ἐν τῷ οϛʹ
entries.evidence: οϛʹ; Eng 77:1-2 'I cried out to God... in the day of my trouble I sought the Lord'

entries.situation: When enemies defile the house of God, kill the saints and leave their bodies to the birds: suffer with the sufferers and plead with God, without being cowed
entries.greek: μιάνωσι τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Θεοῦ ... τὰ σώματα αὐτῶν ῥίψωσι τοῖς πετεινοῖς ... τὸν οηʹ ψαλμόν
entries.evidence: TLG οη (the Migne OCR's 'ογ' is a misread). Eng 79:1-2 defiled temple, bodies given to the birds

entries.situation: Wanting to sing to the Lord at a feast, gathered with His servants
entries.greek: ἐν ἑορτῇ δὲ, θέλων ᾆσαι τῷ Κυρίῳ ... τὰ ἐν τῷ πʹ καὶ ϙδʹ
entries.evidence: πʹ and ϙδʹ; Latin 'octogesimum et nonagesimum quartum'. Eng 81:3 'Sound the horn... on the day of our feast'

entries.situation: Enemies massed from every side, threatening God's house and allied against godliness; do not be disheartened by their numbers and power, this is an anchor of hope
entries.greek: τῶν δὲ ἐχθρῶν πάλιν ἐπισυναχθέντων πάντων πανταχόθεν ... ὥσπερ ἄγκυραν ἐλπίδος τὰ ἐν τῷ πβʹ
entries.evidence: πβʹ in both witnesses; Eng 83:5 'they conspire... they form an alliance against You'

entries.situation: Looking at God's house and His eternal dwellings and longing for them, as the Apostle did
entries.greek: τὸν πόθον ἔχῃς εἰς αὐτά, ὡς εἶχεν ὁ Ἀπόστολος, λέγε καὶ σὺ τὸν πγʹ
entries.evidence: πγʹ; Latin 'octogesimum tertium'; Eng 84:1-2 'How lovely is Your dwelling place... my soul longs'

entries.situation: When the anger has passed and the captivity is over, and you want to give thanks
entries.greek: παυσαμένης δέ ποτε τῆς ὀργῆς, καὶ τῆς αἰχμαλωσίας λυθείσης ... τὰ ἐν τῷ πδʹ καὶ ρκεʹ
entries.evidence: πδʹ, ρκεʹ in both Greek witnesses; Latin '84 et 125'. Eng 85:1 and 126:1 both speak of the LORD restoring captives/fortunes. The English copy's 116 is wrong

entries.situation: Wanting to understand how the Catholic Church differs from schisms, and to put the schismatics to shame
entries.greek: τὴν μὲν διαφορὰν τῆς καθολικῆς Ἐκκλησίας πρὸς τὰ σχίσματα ... τὰ ἐν τῷ πϛʹ
entries.evidence: πϛʹ in TLG, Migne Greek (OCR 'πες’') and Latin 'octogesimum sextum'; Eng 87 on Zion as mother city

entries.situation: Wanting to encourage yourself and others in godliness, showing that hope in God never disappoints and makes the soul unafraid
entries.greek: ὡς εἰς τὸν Θεὸν ἐλπὶς οὔτε καταισχύνει, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἄφοβον τὴν ψυχὴν κατασκευάζει ... τὰ ἐν τῷ ϙʹ
entries.evidence: ϙʹ (koppa, rendered 'ς' in the digital text); Latin 'nonagesimum'; Eng 91:5 'You will not fear the terror of the night'

entries.situation: Wanting to sing on the Sabbath (Saturday)
entries.greek: Ψάλαι θέλεις τῷ Σαββάτῳ; ἔχεις τὸν ϙαʹ
entries.csmv: not printed (the English copy omits this pairing)
entries.evidence: ϙαʹ in TLG and the Migne Greek; Latin 'nonagesimum primum'. Eng 92 superscription: 'A song for the Sabbath day'

entries.situation: Wanting to give thanks on the Lord's Day (Sunday)
entries.greek: Εὐχαριστῆσαι θέλεις τῇ Κυριακῇ; ἔχεις τὸν κγʹ
entries.evidence: κγʹ; the LXX title of Ps 23 assigns it to the first day of the week

entries.situation: Wanting to sing on Monday (the second day of the week)
entries.greek: Ἆσαι θέλεις δευτέρᾳ Σαββάτων; λέγε τὰ ἐν τῷ μζʹ
entries.evidence: μζʹ in both Greek witnesses; Latin '47'. The LXX title of Ps 47 reads 'for the second day of the week'. The English copy's 95 is wrong

entries.situation: Wanting to praise on Friday: a victory song, because at the Cross God's house was built though enemies tried to stop it
entries.greek: Αἰνέσαι βούλει τῇ Παρασκευῇ; ἔχεις τὸν αἶνον ἐν τῷ ϙβʹ
entries.evidence: ϙβʹ; Latin '92'. The LXX title of Ps 92 reads 'for the day before the Sabbath'

entries.situation: When God's house has been torn down in a captivity and then rebuilt
entries.greek: αἰχμαλωσίας γενομένης, καθαιρεθῇ ὁ οἶκος, καὶ πάλιν οἰκοδομηθῇ, ᾆδε τὰ ἐν τῷ ϙεʹ
entries.evidence: ϙεʹ; Latin '95'. The LXX title of Ps 95 reads 'when the house was being built after the captivity'

entries.situation: When the land has rest from war and is at peace, and the Lord reigns
entries.greek: τῆς δὲ γῆς κατάστασιν λαβούσης ἀπὸ τῶν πολεμούντων ... βασιλεύσαντος τοῦ Κυρίου ... τὸν ϙϛʹ
entries.evidence: ϙϛʹ (ςς in digital text); Latin 'nonagesimum sextum'; Eng 97:1 'The LORD reigns'

entries.situation: Wanting to sing on Wednesday, the day the Lord was handed over and began His triumph over death and the devil
entries.greek: Θέλεις τῇ τετράδι τοῦ Σαββάτου ψάλλειν; ἔχεις τὸν ϙγʹ
entries.evidence: ϙγʹ twice; the LXX title of Ps 93 reads 'for the fourth day of the week'; Eng 94:1 'O LORD, God of vengeance'

entries.situation: Seeing the Lord's care and rule over everything and wanting to lead others into faith and obedience, getting them first to give thanks
entries.greek: θέλων κατηχῆσαί τινας εἰς τὴν αὐτοῦ πίστιν καὶ ὑπακοήν, πείθων αὐτοὺς πρῶτον ἐξομολογεῖσθαι, ψάλλε τὸν ϙθʹ
entries.evidence: ϙθʹ; Latin '99'. Eng 100 superscription 'A Psalm of thanksgiving'; 100:3 'Know that the LORD is God'

entries.situation: Having learned that the Lord judges and mixes mercy into His judgment, and wanting to draw near to Him
entries.greek: ὅτι ἐλέῳ τὴν κρίσιν κεράσας κρίνει ὁ Κύριος, θελήσῃς αὐτῷ προσελθεῖν ... τοὺς ἐν τῷ ρʹ
entries.evidence: ρʹ; Latin 'centesimum'; Eng 101:1 'I will sing of Your loving devotion and justice'

entries.situation: Our nature being weak, the pressures of life leave you feeling poor and worn down to the point of listlessness, and you want comfort
entries.greek: διὰ τὰς συνοχὰς τοῦ βίου ὡς πτωχὸς γενόμενος ἀκηδιάσῃς ποτέ, καὶ θέλῃς παρακληθῆναι, ἔχεις τὸν ραʹ
entries.evidence: ραʹ; Latin '101'. The LXX title 'a prayer of the poor man when he is weary (ἀκηδιάσῃ)' matches the letter's own wording; BSB superscription: 'a prayer of one who is afflicted, when he grows faint'

entries.situation: Because we should give thanks in and through everything: blessing God and stirring up your own soul to do it
entries.greek: ὅτε θέλεις εὐλογεῖν αὐτόν, ἔχεις εἰς τοῦτο προτρέπεσθαι σαυτοῦ τὴν ψυχήν ... τὸν ρβʹ καὶ ργʹ
entries.evidence: ρβʹ, ργʹ; both Eng psalms open 'Bless the LORD, O my soul'

entries.situation: Wanting to praise God and to learn how, for what, and with which words
entries.greek: αἰνεῖν θέλεις τὸν Θεόν ... ρδʹ, ρϛʹ, ρλδʹ, ρμεʹ, ρμϛʹ, ρμζʹ, ρμηʹ, ρνʹ
entries.evidence: TLG and the Migne Greek agree; Latin '104, 106, 134, 145, 146, 147, 148, 150'. LXX 146+147 = Eng 147. The English copy adds 113, 117 and 149, which are not in the Greek

entries.situation: Having faith, as the Lord taught, and believing the things you say in prayer
entries.greek: ἔχεις πίστιν ... καὶ πιστεύεις οἷς εὐχόμενος λαλεῖς; λέγε τὸν ριεʹ
entries.evidence: ριεʹ; LXX 115:1 'I believed, therefore I spoke' = Eng 116:10

entries.situation: Sensing yourself climbing upward in how you live, forgetting what is behind and straining ahead; one song for each step forward
entries.greek: ἀναβαίνοντα σαυτὸν αἴσθῃ ταῖς πράξεσιν ... τὰς ιεʹ τῶν ἀναβαθμῶν ᾠδάς
entries.evidence: ιεʹ (fifteen) Songs of Ascents; BSB superscription 'A song of ascents' on Eng 120-134. The English copy prints the LXX numbers

entries.situation: Having been carried off captive by alien thoughts, then noticing and repenting: stop, stay put, sit down and weep as the exiles did
entries.greek: ᾐχμαλωτεύθης ὑπὸ ἀλλοτρίων λογισμῶν ... κάθου, καὶ κλαῦσον ... τὰ ἐν τῷ ρλϛʹ
entries.evidence: ρλϛʹ; Latin '136'; Eng 137:1 'By the rivers of Babylon we sat and wept'

entries.situation: Taking temptations as your testing, and wanting to give thanks once they are past
entries.greek: τοὺς δὲ πειρασμοὺς ἡγούμενος εἶναί σου δοκιμήν ... ἔχεις τὸν ρληʹ
entries.evidence: ρληʹ; Latin '138'; Eng 139:23 'Search me, O God... test me'

entries.situation: Hemmed in by enemies again and wanting to be rescued
entries.greek: συνέχῃ πάλιν ἀπὸ ἐχθρῶν, καὶ ῥυσθῆναι θέλεις; λέγε τὰ ἐν τῷ ρλθʹ
entries.evidence: ρλθʹ; Latin '139'; Eng 140:1 'Rescue me, O LORD, from evil men'

entries.situation: Wanting to pray and plead with God
entries.greek: δεηθῆναι δὲ καὶ προσεύξασθαι θέλεις; ψάλλε τὸν εʹ καὶ ρμβʹ
entries.evidence: εʹ and ρμβʹ in TLG and the Migne Greek. The English copy adds 141, 142 and 146. Eng 143:1 'O LORD, hear my prayer'

entries.situation: A tyrant enemy rising against God's people and against you, as Goliath did against David; do not cower, trust as David did
entries.greek: ἐχθρὸς τύραννος ἐπανέστη τῷ λαῷ καί σοι, ὥσπερ Γολιὰθ τῷ Δαβίδ ... τὰ ἐν τῷ ρμγʹ
entries.evidence: ρμγʹ in the Greek. The LXX title of Ps 143 adds 'against Goliath'; Eng 144:1 'who trains my hands for war'

entries.situation: Marvelling at God's kindness to everyone and remembering His goodness to you, and wanting to bless Him for it
entries.greek: θαυμάζων τὰς εἰς πάντας τοῦ Θεοῦ εὐεργεσίας ... ἐν τῷ ρμδʹ ψαλμῷ
entries.evidence: ρμδʹ in both Greek witnesses. Eng 145:9 'The LORD is good to all'. The English copy's 105 is wrong

entries.situation: Simply wanting to sing to the Lord
entries.greek: Ἆσαι θέλεις τῷ Κυρίῳ; ἔχεις εἰς τὸ λέγειν τὸν ϙβʹ καὶ ϙζʹ
entries.evidence: ϙβʹ and ϙζʹ in TLG and the Migne Greek ('.ιβ' καὶ ζ΄', koppa lost); Latin '92 et 9[7]'. The English copy's 96 does not match the Greek

entries.situation: Being young or small yet chosen to lead your brothers: do not lord it over them, give the glory to the Lord who chose you
entries.greek: ἐὰν μικρὸς ὢν προκριθῇς εἰς ἀρχήν τινα τῶν ἀδελφῶν σου ... τὸν ρναʹ ἴδιον ὄντα τοῦ Δαβίδ
entries.english: none (Psalm 151 is in the Septuagint and Orthodox Bibles only)
entries.evidence: ρναʹ; the LXX Ps 151 is David's short psalm about being the least of his brothers and anointed

entries.situation: Wanting to sing psalms that have 'Alleluia' as their refrain
entries.greek: ψάλλειν ἐπακοὴν ἔχοντας τὸ Ἀλληλούϊα ... ρδʹ ... ρνʹ
entries.evidence: Greek list agrees in TLG and Migne. LXX 111-118 = Eng 112-119 (with LXX 113 = Eng 114-115 and LXX 114-115 = Eng 116). The English copy prints 111-118 unconverted

entries.situation: Psalms about the Saviour: His true begetting from the Father and His coming in the flesh
entries.greek: τὸν μὲν μδʹ καὶ τὸν ρθʹ δηλοῦντας τὴν ἐκ τοῦ Πατρὸς αὐτοῦ γνησίαν γέννησιν
entries.evidence: μδʹ, ρθʹ in both witnesses

entries.situation: Psalms about the Saviour: the Cross, the plotting He bore for us and how much He suffered
entries.greek: τὸν δὲ καʹ καὶ ξηʹ προλέγοντας περὶ τοῦ θείου σταυροῦ
entries.evidence: καʹ, ξηʹ in both witnesses

entries.situation: Psalms about the Saviour: the plotting and malice of the Jewish leaders and the betrayal by Judas Iscariot
entries.greek: τὸν μὲν βʹ καὶ ρηʹ σημαίνοντας τήν τε τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐπιβουλήν ... καὶ τὴν Ἰούδα τοῦ Ἰσκαριώτου προδοσίαν
entries.evidence: βʹ in TLG and the Migne Greek ('τὸν μὲν β' καὶ ρη’'). The English copy's 3 is wrong. Eng 109:8 is quoted of Judas in Acts 1:20

entries.situation: Psalms about the Saviour: His kingship and power to judge, His second coming in the flesh, and the calling of the Gentiles
entries.greek: τόν τε κʹ, καὶ μθʹ, καὶ οαʹ ... τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ καὶ κριτικὴν δύναμιν
entries.evidence: κʹ, μθʹ, οαʹ in both witnesses

entries.situation: Psalms about the Saviour: His resurrection from the dead
entries.greek: ὁ μὲν ιεʹ δείκνυσιν αὐτοῦ τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀνάστασιν
entries.evidence: ιεʹ; Eng 16:10 'You will not abandon my soul to Sheol', applied to the resurrection in Acts 2:27

entries.situation: Psalms about the Saviour: His ascension into heaven
entries.greek: ὁ δὲ κγʹ καὶ μϛʹ ἀπαγγέλλουσι τὴν εἰς οὐρανοὺς ἄνοδον αὐτοῦ
entries.evidence: κγʹ, μϛʹ; Eng 24:7 'Lift up your heads, O gates'; 47:5 'God has ascended amid shouts of joy'

entries.situation: Psalms about the Saviour: the benefits that came to us through His sufferings
entries.greek: τὸν δὲ ϙβʹ, καὶ ϙεʹ, καὶ ϙζʹ, καὶ ϙηʹ ἀναγινώσκων
entries.evidence: four koppa numerals in TLG (ςβ, ςε, ςζ, ςη); the Migne OCR is garbled but consistent

entries.situation: Sadness: grief is eased as you sing asking your own soul why it is so downcast
entries.greek: τὸ δὲ λυποῦν θεραπεύεται ... Ἵνα τί περίλυπος εἶ, ἡ ψυχή μου, καὶ ἵνα τί συνταράσσεις με;
entries.csmv: none printed (the line is quoted without a number)
entries.evidence: No numeral. Identified from the quoted refrain, which is exact LXX wording in all three places; Eng 42:5, 42:11, 43:5 'Why, my soul, are you downcast?'

entries.situation: A slip or failure: you come to admit it as you sing that your feet had nearly slipped
entries.greek: τὸ μὲν ἐσφαλμένον ἐπιγνώσεται λέγουσα· Ἐμοῦ δὲ παρὰ μικρὸν ἐσαλεύθησαν οἱ πόδες
entries.csmv: none printed (the line is quoted without a number)
entries.evidence: No numeral. Identified from the quotation; Eng 73:2 'my feet had almost stumbled; my steps had nearly slipped'

entries.situation: Fear: hope steadies a frightened soul as you sing that the Lord is your helper and you will not fear what people can do
entries.greek: τὸ δὲ φοβηθὲν ἐπιῤῥώσει τῇ ἐλπίδι ... Κύριος ἐμοὶ βοηθός, καὶ οὐ φοβηθήσομαι τί ποιήσει μοι ἄνθρωπος
entries.csmv: none printed (the line is quoted without a number)
entries.evidence: No numeral. The quotation is exact LXX 117:6 (also quoted in Heb 13:6); Eng 118:6 'The LORD is on my side; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?' Eng 56:11 is similar but lacks 'the Lord is my helper'

entries.situation: For anyone who cares for people who suffer, and for yourself when you are a stranger far from home or brought low: meditating on God's words is what saves
entries.greek: ἔλεγεν ἐν τῷ ριηʹ ψαλμῷ ... Ψαλτὰ ἦσάν μοι τὰ δικαιώματά σου ἐν τόπῳ παροικίας μου ... τότε ἂν ἀπωλόμην ἐν τῇ ταπεινώσει μου
entries.evidence: ριηʹ plus three quoted verses; BSB 119:54 'Your statutes are songs to me in the house of my pilgrimage', 119:92 'I would have perished in my affliction'

problems: The letter's full Greek text is reliable to work from: the TLG text as posted by Documenta Catholica Omnia, checked against a scan of Migne PG 27. In that digital text, 'ς' stands for both stigma (6) and koppa (90), so a lone 'ςʹ' can mean 6 or 90. I resolved each one from its place in the numeral and from the psalm's content (e.g. 'τὸν ςʹ καὶ τὸν λζʹ' = 6 and 37; 'τὰ ἐν τῷ ςʹ' for fearless hope = 90).

Two places where the TLG text and Migne's scan disagree: the TLG gives ιϛ (16) for 'saved from your enemies' and πϛ (86) in the prayer-against-opponents list. Migne's Greek and Latin both read ιζ (17) and πζ (87), and those match the psalms themselves (Eng 18 superscription; Eng 88 is a prayer, Eng 87 is about Zion). I used Migne's numbers and marked both entries medium confidence.

Errors in the English copy (marcellinus.txt) on top of the three already spotted: §12 prints '11 and 12' (should be 12 and 17); the vintage song '8 or 19' (should be 8 and 84); prayer against opponents '140' (should be 141); the thanksgiving list adds 71 and 126, which are not in the Greek; after the captivity '116' (should be 126); Monday '95' (should be 48); the praise list adds 113, 117 and 149; prayer and supplication '5, 141-143, 146' (Greek has only 5 and 143 in English numbering); God's kindness to all '105' (should be 145); 'sing to the Lord' '96 and 98' (Greek gives Eng 93 and 98); the Alleluia list prints LXX 111-118 without converting (should be 112-119); the plot and Judas psalms '3 and 109' (should be 2 and 109); the Gradual Psalms '119-133' twice (should be 120-134).

The English copy leaves out one pairing altogether: 'Do you want to sing on the Sabbath? You have the 91st' (LXX 91 = Eng 92, 'A song for the Sabbath day'). In the Greek it comes just before the Lord's Day pairing.

The English copy's §12 puts 'Psalm 51' on the conscience-stricken repentance clause, where the Greek names no psalm. The Greek names ν (50 = Eng 51) a sentence later, as the person's own words of repentance. The pairing stands; only its place in the sentence differs.

Not listed as entries because they classify or describe psalms rather than pair them with a situation: §14's catalogue of psalm types (narrative, prayer, petition, thanksgiving, exhortation, prophecy, blessing, 'accusing the ungodly', and so on, with long numeral lists; the English copy shortens it and gets it wrong), and §§2-9's survey of which psalms retell Genesis, the Exodus, the judges, the kings and exile, and which foretell Christ. They can be extracted from the same Greek file if needed.

Several pairings make sense only through the Septuagint superscription, which English Bibles lack or word differently: Ps 7 (LXX title names 'Chousi', i.e. Hushai against Ahithophel; BSB says 'Cush, a Benjamite'); Pss 8 and 84 ('for the winepresses'; BSB 'According to Gittith'); Ps 27 ('before he was anointed'); Ps 66 ('of resurrection'); Pss 24, 48, 93, 94 (days of the week); Ps 96 ('when the house was built after the captivity'); Ps 97 ('when his land is restored'); Ps 102 ('a prayer of the poor when he is weary', close to the BSB); Ps 144 ('against Goliath'). A result page that uses one of these must explain the link, not assume the reader will see it.

In the §21 entry 'when you need exomologesis', the word means giving thanks or acknowledging God openly (every psalm listed is a 'give thanks' psalm), not confessing sin. The C.S.M.V. wording 'testify concerning God' is loose. Confession of sin is the separate LXX 50 (Eng 51) entry.
Psalm 151 (being small but chosen to lead) is only in the Septuagint and Orthodox Bibles; Protestant and Catholic Bibles have no equivalent, and the BSB file has no text for it.

Section numbers come from Migne's section markers, read in the scan (§15 before 'blessed', §16 before Ps 8, §17 before the prayer list, §18 before 'hated by friends', §19 before LXX 38, §20 before 'you have sinned', §21 before 'hymn', §23 before the Lord's Day, §24 before LXX 101, §25 before 'captive to alien thoughts', §26 the Saviour psalms, §28 the sadness/failure/fear lines, §33 Psalm 118/119). The §22 marker OCR'd poorly; I placed it at the festival pairing, which fits the sequence.

Scriptural fit that is weak even though the Greek is certain: LXX 11 (Eng 12) as an expression of 'trust' in §12; LXX 92 (Eng 93, 'The LORD reigns') for simply wanting to sing to the Lord. Neither is a numbering error.

Pairings best suited to a feelings-based quiz (a person's state, not doctrine or a liturgical occasion), in English numbering: 13 (forgotten by God, opposition that never ends), 42 (longing for God, hope), 102 (worn down, poor, listless), 51 (sin and shame), 73 (the wicked prosper), 55 (betrayed by friends), 31 (rejected by family and friends), 3 (turned on by your own), 37 (envying the wicked), 40 (patience in hardship), 23 (being shepherded), 27 (outnumbered), 62 (under fierce attack, submitting to God), 63 (alone in a wilderness), 137 (carried off by wrong thoughts), 139 (tested), 116:10-19 (faith in prayer), 91 (fearless hope), 46 and 18 (rescued, thankful), 145 (overwhelmed by God's goodness), 6/38 (under God's displeasure), 11 (being frightened), 12 (evil everywhere), 77 (cornered, near despair), the Songs of Ascents (growing), plus the §28 verses for sadness (42:5), failure (73:2) and fear (118:6).

englishCat.greekSource: READ DIRECTLY. The Greek text is the TLG digitisation (TLG 2035.059, the Migne PG 27:12-45 text), posted as a PDF by Documenta Catholica Omnia: http://www.documentacatholicaomnia.eu/02g/0295-0373,_Athanasius,_Epistula_ad_Marcellinum_de_interpretatione_Psalmorum,_MGR.pdf (the index page is http://www.documentacatholicaomnia.eu/04z/z_0295-0373__Athanasius__Epistula_ad_Marcellinum_de_interpretatione_Psalmorum__MGR.pdf.html). WebFetch failed on a certificate error, so I piped the PDF through pypdf and saved only the extracted text to the scratchpad (marc-greek.txt, sents2.txt). I read every numeral in the catalogue (§§15-26), in §12, in §14, in §§3-8 and in the closing section. One extraction caveat: stigma (ϛ = 6) and koppa (ϙ = 90) came out as a stray 'ς' on a line of its own. I put them back by position: in front of a units letter, or standing alone, the stray letter is koppa; after a tens letter it is stigma. For example ϙγ = 93, κϛ = 26 and ϙ alone = 90. Two independent cross-checks: (1) the modern Greek EPE translation (Έλληνες Πατέρες της Εκκλησίας, Αθανασίου Άπαντα 5, Ερμηνευτικά Α΄, Gregorios o Palamas, 1975, pp. 40-59; §§15-26 only, LXX numbers), at https://greekdownloads.wordpress.com/2022/07/22/μέγας-αθανάσιος-ποιόν-ψαλμό-του-δαβίδ/ ; (2) the same C.S.M.V. translation with its original Septuagint numbers, at https://www.fisheaters.com/psalmsathanasiusletter.html . Comparing it with the scratchpad copy shows the copy's errors come from two places: the translation's own misreadings, and the later conversion to English numbering. Not obtained: Gregg's 1980 Paulist translation (I found no online text; Amazon and Google Books listings only) and the Savvidis-Wyrwa critical edition (De Gruyter). I searched for Scribd and blog tables; they either reproduce the C.S.M.V. or are behind a login.

entries.situation: Singing a psalm stirs repentance in the singer and in those who hear it.
entries.greek: τὸν νʹ ψαλμὸν ... τῆς μετανοίας
entries.evidence: Greek νʹ = 50. The superscription of Eng 51 names Nathan after Bathsheba. Content: 'Have mercy on me, O God'.

entries.situation: A person singing it has their own troubles in mind and finds the words are their own.
entries.greek: τὸν τρίτον ψάλλει ... εἰς τὰς ἰδίας θλίψεις
entries.evidence: Greek τὸν τρίτον. Content: 3:1 'how many are my foes'.

entries.situation: Speaking your own trust in God and your own prayer.
entries.greek: τὸν ιαʹ καὶ τὸν ιϛʹ ὡς εἰς τὴν ἰδίαν πεποίθησιν καὶ προσευχήν
entries.english: 12, 17 (by the TLG Greek); 11, 12 if the C.S.M.V. reading is right
entries.evidence: The TLG Greek reads ιαʹ and ιϛʹ (11, 16). §14 of the same text lists ιϛʹ first among the psalms 'as prayer', and LXX 16 is titled 'A prayer of David' (Eng 17), so the reading is internally coherent. The C.S.M.V. (fisheaters, LXX numbers) reads 10 and 11 = Eng 11 ('In the LORD I take refuge') and 12 ('Help, O LORD'). Both fit. The editions disagree and I could not see Gregg.

entries.situation: Singing about persecution as if it were your own experience of being hunted, not someone else's.
entries.greek: τὸν νγʹ, καὶ τὸν νεʹ, καὶ τὸν νϛʹ, καὶ τὸν ρμαʹ ... ὡς ὢν ὁ πάσχων
entries.evidence: Greek numerals are explicit. Superscriptions: 54 the Ziphites, 56 seized in Gath, 57 and 142 in the cave.

entries.situation: Psalms written as narrative.
entries.greek: οἱ ἐν διηγήματι ιηʹ, μγʹ, μηʹ, μθʹ, οβʹ, οϛʹ, οζʹ, πηʹ, ρϛʹ, ριγʹ, ρκϛʹ, ρλϛʹ
entries.evidence: TLG Greek list. The C.S.M.V. heavily abridges §14 and prints only a correct subset.

entries.situation: Psalms that exhort or urge the hearer on.
entries.greek: ἐν παραινέσει λϛʹ; προτρεπτικοὶ κηʹ, λβʹ, πʹ, ϙδʹ, ϙεʹ, ϙϛʹ, ϙζʹ, ρβʹ, ργʹ, ριγʹ
entries.evidence: Greek has λβʹ (LXX 32 = Eng 33), not LXX 31. The C.S.M.V. read 31, so the copy's '32' should be 33. The copy's 97 and 103 are correct.

entries.situation: Psalms that are prophecy.
entries.greek: ἐν προφητείᾳ κʹ, καʹ, μδʹ, μϛʹ, οεʹ; ἀπαγγελτικὸς μετὰ προφητείας ρθʹ
entries.evidence: TLG Greek list. The copy prints a correct subset.

entries.situation: Psalms that are prayers or supplications to God.
entries.greek: ὡς ἐν εὐχῇ ιϛʹ, ξζʹ, πθʹ, ραʹ, ρλαʹ, ρμαʹ; ἐν ἐντυχίᾳ καὶ εὐχῇ καὶ δεήσει εʹ, ϛʹ ...
entries.evidence: The copy's four (LXX 6, 15, 53, 101) all appear in the Greek lists. The rest of the Greek lists are omitted by the C.S.M.V.

entries.situation: Psalms of 'confession' in the sense of giving thanks and acknowledging God.
entries.greek: ἐν ἐξομολογήσει θʹ, οδʹ, ϙαʹ, ρδʹ, ρεʹ, ρϛʹ, ρζʹ, ριʹ, ριζʹ, ρλεʹ, ρλζʹ
entries.evidence: In the Greek, ἐξομολόγησις here means thankful acknowledgement. Every listed psalm opens with, or features, 'I will give thanks' or 'Give thanks to the LORD'. Psalm 50 LXX (Eng 51) is NOT in this list. The C.S.M.V. rendered the word 'confessions' and supplied 51.

entries.situation: Psalms that accuse the wicked and lawless.
entries.greek: κατηγορικοὶ τῶν ἀσεβῶν ... βʹ, ιγʹ, λεʹ, ναʹ, νβʹ
entries.evidence: TLG Greek list. The copy gives one correct item.

entries.situation: Psalms of thanksgiving and of praise.
entries.greek: εὐχαριστικοί ηʹ, θʹ, ιζʹ, λγʹ, μεʹ, ξβʹ, οϛʹ, πδʹ, ριδʹ, ριεʹ, ρκʹ, ρκαʹ, ρκγʹ, ρκεʹ, ρκηʹ, ρμγʹ; αἶνον ἀπαγγέλλοντες ... ριβʹ, ριϛʹ, ρλδʹ, ρμδʹ ...
entries.evidence: 8 and 117 are confirmed in the Greek lists. I could not find 98 (LXX 97) or 125 (LXX 124) in the lists as extracted; one praise numeral was lost in extraction.

entries.situation: A shout of joy that speaks of the Resurrection.
entries.greek: ἀλαλαγμοῦ καὶ περὶ ἀναστάσεως ξεʹ
entries.evidence: Greek ξεʹ. The LXX superscription of 65 is 'a psalm of resurrection'. Eng 66 opens 'Shout joyfully to God'.

entries.situation: When you want to call someone blessed, these show how, why and in what words.
entries.greek: μακαρίσαι ... αʹ, λαʹ, μʹ, ριαʹ, ριηʹ, ρκζʹ
entries.evidence: All six open with 'Blessed'. The Greek numerals match.

entries.situation: To rebuke the plot of the Jews against the Saviour.
entries.greek: τὴν Ἰουδαίων κατὰ τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἐπιβουλὴν, ἔχεις τὴν δευτέραν ᾠδήν
entries.evidence: Greek 'the second'. Content: 2:1-2, rulers taking counsel against the LORD and His Anointed.

entries.situation: When your own family turns on you and many rise up against you.
entries.greek: διώκῃ παρὰ τῶν ἰδίων ... λέγε τὸν γʹ
entries.evidence: Superscription: 'when he fled from his son Absalom'. Content: 3:1.

entries.situation: When you called on God in trouble, He heard you, and you want to thank Him.
entries.greek: θλιβόμενος ἐπεκαλέσω ... εἰσακουσθεὶς θέλεις εὐχαριστεῖν, ψάλλε τὸν τέταρτον, καὶ οδʹ, καὶ ριδʹ
entries.evidence: LXX 114 = Eng 116:1-9 ('He has heard my voice'). The copy's '116' is right but should be limited to verses 1-9. Content: 4:1 'answer me when I call'; 75:1 'We give thanks to You'.

entries.situation: When the wicked are lying in wait for you and you want your prayer heard: rise early and sing it.
entries.greek: ἐνεδρεύειν θέλοντας ... ὀρθρίζων τὸ πρωῒ ψάλλε τὸν εʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 5:3 'in the morning You hear my voice'.

entries.situation: When you sense God's threat or displeasure and are shaken by it.
entries.greek: Αἰσθόμενος δὲ ἀπειλῆς τοῦ Κυρίου ... τὸν ϛʹ καὶ τὸν λζʹ
entries.evidence: Both open 'O LORD, rebuke me not in Your anger'.

entries.situation: When people plot against you, as Ahithophel did against David, and someone tells you of it: trust the God Who rescues.
entries.greek: ὡς ὁ Ἀχιτόφελ κατὰ τοῦ Δαβὶδ ... ψάλλε τὸν ζʹ
entries.evidence: Superscription: 'concerning the words of Cush' (LXX Chousi, i.e. Hushai, who brought David word of Ahithophel's counsel).

entries.situation: Seeing the Saviour's grace spread everywhere and the human race saved, and wanting to address the Lord.
entries.greek: τὴν πανταχοῦ χάριν τοῦ Σωτῆρος ... ψάλλε τὸν ηʹ
entries.evidence: Greek ηʹ. Content: 8:1, 8:4-6.

entries.situation: Thanking the Lord in song for the grape harvest.
entries.greek: ᾆσαι θέλεις ἐπιλήνιον ... τὸν ηʹ καὶ τὸν πγʹ
entries.evidence: The Greek reads πγʹ (83), and the EPE translation agrees (8 and 83). Superscriptions: LXX 8 and 83 are both headed 'for the winepresses'; the Hebrew 'according to Gittith' stands on Eng 8, 81 and 84. The C.S.M.V. misread the numeral as 18, hence the copy's 19.

entries.situation: For the defeat of the enemy and the saving of creation: take no credit, knowing the Son of God did it.
entries.greek: κατηργῆσθαι τὸν ἐχθρὸν ... λέγε τὸν εἰς αὐτὸν εἰρημένον θʹ ψαλμόν
entries.evidence: LXX 9 = Eng 9 and 10. Content: 9:3-6, enemies turn back and perish.

entries.situation: When someone is trying hard to frighten or unsettle you: keep trusting the Lord.
entries.greek: λίαν σέ τις ταράσσειν ἐθέλῃ ... ψάλλε τὸν ιʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 11:1 'In the LORD I take refuge; how can you say to me, Flee like a bird'.

entries.situation: When pride and wickedness are everywhere and nothing holy seems left among people: take refuge in the Lord.
entries.greek: μηδὲν ὅσιον ἐπ' ἀνθρώποις ... λέγε τὸν ιαʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 12:1 'the godly are no more'.

entries.situation: When the enemies' plotting drags on and on: do not lose heart as if God had forgotten you, but call on Him.
entries.greek: Ἐγχρονιζούσης ... μὴ ὀλιγώρει ὡς ἐπιλησθεὶς παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ ... ᾄδων τὸν ιβʹ
entries.evidence: The Greek reads ιβʹ (12), and the EPE translation agrees. Content: 13:1 'How long, O LORD? Will You forget me forever?'. The C.S.M.V. itself printed 26 (LXX), apparently a misreading; the copy converted it to 27.

entries.situation: When you hear people blaspheme God's providence: do not join in, but intercede.
entries.greek: βλασφημούντων ... κατὰ τῆς Προνοίας ... τὸν ιγʹ καὶ νβʹ
entries.evidence: Both open 'The fool says in his heart, There is no God'.

entries.situation: To learn what kind of person is a citizen of the kingdom of heaven.
entries.greek: ὁποῖός ἐστι τῆς βασιλείας τῶν οὐρανῶν ὁ πολίτης, ψάλλε τὸν ιδʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 15:1 'who may dwell on Your holy mountain?'.

entries.situation: When you need to pray because of those who oppose you and close in around your soul.
entries.greek: διὰ τοὺς ἀνθεστηκότας σοι καὶ περιέχοντάς σου τὴν ψυχὴν, ᾆδε τὸν ιϛʹ, καὶ τὸν πεʹ, καὶ τὸν πϛʹ(?), καὶ τὸν ρμʹ
entries.evidence: The Greek (TLG) and the EPE translation both read ρμʹ (140) = Eng 141 ('let my prayer be set before You'). The C.S.M.V. read 139, hence the copy's 140. The third numeral reads πϛʹ (86 = Eng 87, a Zion hymn) in the TLG. EPE and the C.S.M.V. both read 87 = Eng 88 ('my soul is full of troubles'), which fits a prayer. 17:9 'my deadly enemies who surround me' matches the Greek περιέχοντας.

entries.situation: If you want to learn how Moses prayed.
entries.greek: πῶς Μωϋσῆς προσηύξατο, ἔχεις τὸν πθʹ
entries.evidence: Superscription: 'A prayer of Moses the man of God'.

entries.situation: When you have been saved from your enemies and rescued from those who hunted you.
entries.greek: ἐσώθης ἀπὸ τῶν ἐχθρῶν σου, καὶ ἐῤῥύσθης ἀπὸ τῶν διωκόντων σε
entries.evidence: Superscription of Eng 18: sung on the day the LORD delivered him from all his enemies and from Saul. The EPE translation and the C.S.M.V. read 17. The TLG numeral reads ιϛʹ (16), apparently a slip in that text, since LXX 16 is a plea, not a thanksgiving.

entries.situation: When you marvel at the order of creation, God's providence in it, and the holy commands of His law.
entries.greek: Θαυμάζεις τὴν τῆς κτίσεως τάξιν ... τοῦ τε νόμου τὰ ἱερὰ προστάγματα, ψάλλε τὸν ιηʹ καὶ τὸν κγʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 19:1 the heavens, and 19:7-11 the law; 24:1-2 the earth is the LORD's.

entries.situation: When you see others in distress: comfort them and pray over them with its words.
entries.greek: Θλιβομένους δὲ ὁρῶν, παρακάλει τούτους ... ιθʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 20:1 'May the LORD answer you in the day of trouble'.

entries.situation: When you see yourself shepherded and led well by the Lord, and rejoice in it.
entries.greek: ποιμαινόμενον καὶ εὐοδούμενον παρὰ τοῦ Κυρίου ... κβʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 23:1 'The LORD is my shepherd'.

entries.situation: When enemies are all around you: lift your soul to God.
entries.greek: Οἱ ἐχθροὶ περὶ σὲ, ἀλλὰ σὺ τὴν ψυχὴν ἐπαίρων πρὸς Θεὸν, λέγε τὸν κδʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 25:1 'To You, O LORD, I lift up my soul'; 25:2, 19 enemies.

entries.situation: When enemies persist, hands full of blood, seeking to destroy you: do not hand judgement to people, but ask God, the only just One, to judge.
entries.greek: μὴ δῷς ἀνθρώπῳ τὸ κρῖμα ... τὸν Θεὸν ἀξιῶν κριτὴν ... κεʹ, λδʹ, μβʹ
entries.evidence: All open 'Vindicate me' or 'Contend, O LORD'.

entries.situation: When enemies attack harder, massed like an army, scorning you as not yet anointed: do not cower.
entries.greek: πλῆθος ὡς παρεμβολαὶ ... ὡς μήπω σου χρισθέντος ... ᾆδε τὸν κϛʹ
entries.evidence: The LXX superscription of 26 is 'of David, before he was anointed'. Content: 27:3 'though an army encamp against me'.

entries.situation: When plotters keep at it shamelessly and human weakness shows: ignore them and cry out to God.
entries.greek: ἀναισχυντῶσιν οἱ ἐπιβουλεύοντες ... κράζε πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν ... κζʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 28:1 'To You, O LORD, I call'.

entries.situation: To learn, with spiritual understanding, how thanks should be offered to the Lord.
entries.greek: εὐχαριστῶν μαθεῖν πῶς δεῖ προσφέρειν τῷ Κυρίῳ ... κηʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 29:1-2 'Ascribe to the LORD glory'. LXX title: 'at the going out of the tabernacle' (cited in §3 too).

entries.situation: When dedicating your house, both your soul that receives the Lord and the bodily house you live in.
entries.greek: ἐγκαινίζων τὸν οἶκόν σου ... κθʹ καὶ τὸν ἐν τοῖς ἀναβαθμοῖς ρκϛʹ
entries.evidence: Superscription of Eng 30: 'for the dedication of the temple (house)'. 127:1 'Unless the LORD builds the house'.

entries.situation: When all your friends and relatives hate and hound you for the truth: do not shrink, look away to what is coming.
entries.greek: διὰ τὴν ἀλήθειαν μισούμενον ... παρὰ πάντων τῶν τε φίλων καὶ συγγενῶν ... λʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 31:11 'a dread to my friends'; 31:5.

entries.situation: When you see people baptized and set free: wonder at God's love for mankind and sing it over them.
entries.greek: Τοὺς δὲ βαπτιζομένους ... λαʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 32:1 'Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven'.

entries.situation: When you want to sing with many others, gathering the upright.
entries.greek: ψάλλειν μετὰ πολλῶν ... τοὺς δικαίους ἄνδρας ... λβʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 33:1 'Sing joyfully to the LORD, O righteous ones'.

entries.situation: When you fell among enemies but slipped away wisely: gather gentle people and give thanks with them.
entries.greek: σοφῶς αὐτοὺς διαφυγὼν ... συγκαλέσας τοὺς πραεῖς ἄνδρας ... λγʹ
entries.evidence: Superscription: 'when he pretended to be insane before Abimelech'. 34:2-3 'the humble will hear... magnify the LORD with me'.

entries.situation: When you see how keen the lawless are on evil: do not think evil is in their nature, as heretics say; they are the cause of their own sin.
entries.greek: μὴ νόμιζε ἐν αὐτοῖς κατὰ φύσιν τὴν κακίαν εἶναι, οἷα λέγουσιν οἱ αἱρετικοί ... λεʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 36:1-4, the wicked man plotting on his bed and setting himself on a bad path.

entries.situation: When the wicked do much wrong and lord it over the small: tell yourself and others not to heed or envy them, for they soon fade.
entries.greek: μηδὲ παραζηλοῦν αὐτοὺς, διὰ τὸ ταχέως αὐτοὺς ἀποσβέννυσθαι ... λϛʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 37:1-2 'Do not fret... do not envy... they wither quickly'.

entries.situation: When you have resolved to watch yourself and see the enemy attacking, and want to brace yourself against him.
entries.greek: προθέμενος προσέχειν σαυτῷ ... ληʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 39:1 'I will guard my ways... while the wicked are before me'.

entries.situation: When under attack you are bearing troubles and want to learn what patient endurance gains.
entries.greek: ὑπομένῃς τὰς θλίψεις ... τὴν ἐκ τῆς ὑπομονῆς ὠφέλειαν ... λθʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 40:1 'I waited patiently for the LORD'.

entries.situation: When you see many poor people: commend those who have given and urge others to give.
entries.greek: πολλοὺς πένητας καὶ πτωχοὺς ... μʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 41:1 'Blessed is he who cares for the poor'.

entries.situation: When you long wholly for God and enemies mock you: comfort your soul with hope in God and ease its griefs.
entries.greek: πάνυ τὸν πόθον ἔχων εἰς τὸν Θεὸν ... ὀνειδιζόντων ... μαʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 42:1-3 the deer; 'Where is your God?'.

entries.situation: To keep remembering God's kindness to the fathers in the exodus and the desert, how good He is and how ungrateful people are.
entries.greek: τὰς εὐεργεσίας τοῦ Θεοῦ τὰς γενομένας εἰς τοὺς πατέρας ... μγʹ, οζʹ, πηʹ, ρδʹ, ρεʹ, ρϛʹ, ριγʹ
entries.evidence: Greek list. LXX 113 = Eng 114 + 115.

entries.situation: After fleeing to God and being rescued from surrounding troubles, to thank Him and tell of His kindness to you.
entries.greek: διασωθεὶς ἀπὸ τῶν περὶ σὲ γενομένων θλίψεων ... μεʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 46:1 'God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble'.

entries.situation: When you have sinned, are ashamed, are turning back and asking for mercy.
entries.greek: ἥμαρτες, καὶ ἐντραπεὶς μεταγινώσκεις ... νʹ
entries.evidence: Superscription: Nathan after Bathsheba.

entries.situation: When you have been slandered before a wicked ruler and see the slanderer gloating: withdraw and pray it.
entries.greek: διεβλήθης πονηρῷ βασιλεῖ ... ναʹ
entries.evidence: Superscription: Doeg the Edomite informing Saul. 52:1 'Why do you boast of evil?'.

entries.situation: When you are hunted and people inform on you to hand you over, as the Ziphites and the foreigners did to David: do not despair, trust and praise.
entries.greek: ὡς οἱ Ζιφαῖοι καὶ οἱ ἀλλόφυλοι τὸν Δαβὶδ ... νγʹ καὶ νεʹ
entries.evidence: Superscriptions: 54 the Ziphites; 56 seized by the Philistines in Gath.

entries.situation: When the pursuer, unknowing, enters the very cave where you are hiding: even then, do not be afraid.
entries.greek: εἰσέλθῃ εἰς τὸ σπήλαιον ἐν ᾧ καὶ σὺ κρύπτῃ ... νϛʹ ... ρμαʹ
entries.evidence: Superscriptions: 57 'when he fled from Saul into the cave'; 142 'when he was in the cave'.

entries.situation: When the plotter has your house watched and you escape: thank the Lord and engrave the memory on your soul.
entries.greek: φυλαχθῆναι τὴν οἰκίαν ... καὶ διαφύγῃς ... νηʹ
entries.evidence: Superscription: 'when Saul sent men to watch David's house to kill him'.

entries.situation: When enemies taunt you and people who seemed to be friends slander you, and it hurts for a while: praise God and be comforted.
entries.greek: οἱ δοκοῦντες εἶναι φίλοι ... νδʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 55:12-14, 'it is not an enemy who taunts me... but you, my companion'.

entries.situation: Against hypocrites and those who boast in appearances, to put them to shame.
entries.greek: πρὸς μὲν ὑποκρινομένους ... νζʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 58:1-2, 'Do you indeed speak justly?... in your hearts you devise injustice'.

entries.situation: When people rush at you savagely and want your life: set your submission to God against them; the fiercer they rage, the more yield to the Lord.
entries.greek: θέλοντας λαβεῖν σου τὴν ψυχὴν, ἀντίθες σὺ τὴν πρὸς τὸν Θεόν σου ὑποταγὴν ... ξαʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 62:1-3 'In God alone my soul finds rest... How long will you threaten a man?' (LXX 61:2 'οὐχὶ τῷ θεῷ ὑποταγήσεται ἡ ψυχή μου').

entries.situation: When persecution drives you into the wilderness: do not fear being alone, for God is there; sing to Him at dawn.
entries.greek: διωκόμενος εἰς ἐρημίαν ... ὀρθρίζων ψάλλε τὸν ξβʹ
entries.evidence: Superscription: 'when he was in the Wilderness of Judah'. 63:1 'earnestly I seek You'.

entries.situation: When enemies keep terrifying you and never stop laying traps, however many they are: do not give way; their blows will be like children's arrows.
entries.greek: βέλη γὰρ νηπίων ἔσονται τούτων αἱ πληγαὶ ... ξγʹ, ξδʹ, ξθʹ, οʹ
entries.evidence: The 'arrows of infants' phrase is LXX 63:8 = Eng 64:7, which confirms the conversion.

entries.situation: Whenever you want to sing a hymn of praise to the Lord.
entries.greek: ὑμνῆσαι βούλῃ τὸν Κύριον, ᾆδε τὰ ἐν τῷ ξδʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 65:1 'Praise awaits You, O God, in Zion'.

entries.situation: To teach someone about the resurrection.
entries.greek: κατηχῆσαι θέλῃς τινὰς περὶ ἀναστάσεως ... ξεʹ
entries.evidence: The LXX superscription of 65 is 'a psalm of resurrection'.

entries.situation: When asking God for mercy, praise Him as you ask.
entries.greek: Οἰκτιρμοὺς δὲ αἰτῶν ... ξϛʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 67:1 'May God be gracious to us and bless us'.

entries.situation: When the wicked live in ease and peace while the righteous suffer: so that you are not scandalised or shaken.
entries.greek: τοὺς μὲν ἀσεβεῖς ἐν εἰρήνῃ εὐθηνουμένους ... τοὺς δὲ δικαίους θλιβομένους ... οβʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 73:3 'I envied the arrogant when I saw the prosperity of the wicked'.

entries.situation: When God is angry with His people: wise words of comfort.
entries.greek: ὀργισθῇ ὁ Θεὸς ἐπὶ τὸν λαὸν ... ογʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 74:1 'Why does Your anger burn against the sheep of Your pasture?'.

entries.situation: When you need to give thankful acknowledgement to God (C.S.M.V.: 'testify').
entries.greek: χρεία σοι ἐξομολογήσεώς ... θʹ, οδʹ, ϙαʹ, ρδʹ, ρεʹ, ρϛʹ, ρζʹ, ριʹ, ριζʹ, ρλεʹ, ρλζʹ
entries.evidence: The Greek lists eleven psalms; 71 (LXX 70) and 126 (LXX 125) are not among them. Every listed psalm opens with or features 'I will give thanks' or 'Give thanks' (ἐξομολογ-), which confirms the list. The EPE translation prints 115 for 117, a misprint by the same test.

entries.situation: To show pagans and heretics that the true knowledge of God is not with them but only in the catholic Church.
entries.greek: δυσωπῆσαι ... τὰ τῶν Ἑλλήνων καὶ τὰ τῶν αἱρετικῶν ... οεʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 76:1 'God is known in Judah'.

entries.situation: When enemies have cut off your ways of escape and you are hard pressed and shaken: do not despair but pray; when your cry is heard, give thanks.
entries.greek: προκαταλαβόντων τὰς διεκφυγὰς ... μὴ ἀπελπίσῃς ... οϛʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 77:1-2 'I cried out to God... He heard me; in the day of my trouble I sought the Lord'.

entries.situation: When God's house is defiled, His saints killed and their bodies thrown to the birds: suffer with the sufferers and plead for them.
entries.greek: μιάνωσι τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Θεοῦ ... ῥίψωσι τοῖς πετεινοῖς ... οηʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 79:1-2, the temple defiled and the bodies given to the birds.

entries.situation: On a feast day, gathering the servants of God to sing to the Lord together.
entries.greek: Ἐν ἑορτῇ ... πʹ καὶ ϙδʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 81:3 'on the day of our feast'; 95:1 'Come, let us sing'.

entries.situation: When enemies gather from everywhere, threaten God's house and make pacts against true religion: do not lose heart at their numbers; this is an anchor of hope.
entries.greek: ἐπισυναχθέντων πάντων πανταχόθεν ... ὥσπερ ἄγκυραν ἐλπίδος ... πβʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 83:2-5, 'they conspire... they form an alliance against You'.

entries.situation: When you look at God's house and His eternal dwellings and long for them, as the Apostle did.
entries.greek: τὸν πόθον ἔχῃς εἰς αὐτὰ ... πγʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 84:1-2 'How lovely is Your dwelling place... my soul longs'.

entries.situation: When at last the wrath has passed and captivity is ended, and you want to give thanks.
entries.greek: Παυσαμένης δέ ποτε τῆς ὀργῆς, καὶ τῆς αἰχμαλωσίας λυθείσης ... πδʹ καὶ ρκεʹ
entries.evidence: The Greek reads ρκεʹ (125), and the EPE translation agrees. Content: 85:1-3 'You restored Jacob from captivity... You withdrew all Your fury'; 126:1 'When the LORD restored the captives of Zion'. The C.S.M.V. printed LXX 114-115, hence the copy's 116.

entries.situation: To see the difference between the catholic Church and schisms, and to shame the schismatics.
entries.greek: τὴν διαφορὰν τῆς καθολικῆς Ἐκκλησίας πρὸς τὰ σχίσματα ... πϛʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 87, Zion as the mother of the peoples.

entries.situation: To encourage yourself and others in reverence for God, and to show that hope in God does not disappoint but makes the soul fearless.
entries.greek: ἄφοβον τὴν ψυχὴν κατασκευάζει ... τῷ ϙʹ
entries.evidence: Greek ϙʹ = 90 (EPE agrees). Content: 91:5 'You will not fear the terror of the night'.

entries.situation: Singing on the Sabbath (Saturday).
entries.greek: Ψάλαι θέλεις τῷ Σαββάτῳ; ἔχεις τὸν ϙαʹ
entries.csmv: not printed (the English copy omits this sentence)
entries.evidence: The Greek and the EPE translation both have it. Superscription of Eng 92: 'A song for the Sabbath day'.

entries.situation: Giving thanks on the Lord's Day (Sunday).
entries.greek: Εὐχαριστῆσαι θέλεις τῇ Κυριακῇ; ἔχεις τὸν κγʹ
entries.evidence: The LXX superscription of 23 reads 'of the first day of the week'.

entries.situation: Singing on Monday (the second day of the week).
entries.greek: Ἆσαι θέλεις δευτέρᾳ Σαββάτων; λέγε τὰ ἐν τῷ μζʹ
entries.evidence: The Greek reads μζʹ (47), and the EPE translation agrees ('47ο'). The LXX superscription of 47 reads 'for the second day of the week'. The C.S.M.V. printed 94, hence the copy's 95.

entries.situation: Praise on Friday: at the crucifixion God's house was built in spite of the enemy, so a victory song fits.
entries.greek: Αἰνέσαι βούλει τῇ Παρασκευῇ; ... ϙβʹ ... ἐπινίκιον
entries.evidence: The LXX superscription of 92 reads 'for the day before the Sabbath, when the land was settled'.

entries.situation: When God's house has been destroyed in captivity and then rebuilt.
entries.greek: αἰχμαλωσίας γενομένης, καθαιρεθῇ ὁ οἶκος, καὶ πάλιν οἰκοδομηθῇ ... ϙεʹ
entries.evidence: The LXX superscription of 95 reads 'when the house was being built after the captivity'.

entries.situation: When the land is at rest from war and the Lord reigns.
entries.greek: Τῆς δὲ γῆς κατάστασιν λαβούσης ... βασιλεύσαντος τοῦ Κυρίου ... ϙϛʹ
entries.evidence: The LXX superscription of 96 reads 'when his land is established'. 97:1 'The LORD reigns'.

entries.situation: Singing on Wednesday, the day the Lord was handed over and the leaders took counsel against Him.
entries.greek: τῇ τετράδι τοῦ Σαββάτου ... ϙγʹ
entries.evidence: The LXX superscription of 93 reads 'for the fourth day of the week'.

entries.situation: Seeing the Lord's providence and rule over all, and wanting to teach others faith and obedience: have them confess Him first.
entries.greek: κατηχῆσαί τινας εἰς τὴν αὐτοῦ πίστιν ... ϙθʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 100:3-4 'Know that the LORD is God... enter His gates with thanksgiving'.

entries.situation: Having learned His power as Judge, and that He mixes judgement with mercy, and wanting to draw near to Him.
entries.greek: ἐλέῳ τὴν κρίσιν κεράσας ... ρʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 101:1 'I will sing of Your loving devotion and justice'.

entries.situation: When our weak nature and the pressures of life leave you feeling poor and dispirited, and you want comfort.
entries.greek: διὰ τὰς συνοχὰς τοῦ βίου ὡς πτωχὸς γενόμενος ἀκηδιάσῃς ... ραʹ
entries.evidence: Superscription of Eng 102: 'A prayer of one who is afflicted, when he grows faint'.

entries.situation: Because we ought to thank God through everything, when you want to bless Him and stir your own soul to it.
entries.greek: διὰ πάντων καὶ ἐν πᾶσιν εὐχαριστεῖν ... ρβʹ καὶ ργʹ
entries.evidence: Both open 'Bless the LORD, O my soul'.

entries.situation: To learn how to praise God, for what, and who should praise Him.
entries.greek: πῶς καὶ ἐπὶ τίνι δεῖ αἰνεῖν ... ρδʹ, ρϛʹ, ρλδʹ, ρμεʹ, ρμϛʹ, ρμζʹ, ρμηʹ, ρνʹ
entries.evidence: The Greek (TLG) and EPE agree on eight numbers. The copy adds 113, 117 and 149, which are not in the Greek.

entries.situation: Do you have faith, as the Lord asked, and believe what you say in prayer?
entries.greek: Ἔχεις πίστιν ... καὶ πιστεύεις οἷς εὐχόμενος λαλεῖς; λέγε τὸν ριεʹ
entries.evidence: LXX 115:1 = Eng 116:10, 'I believed, therefore I said'.

entries.situation: When you sense yourself climbing in how you live, forgetting what lies behind and reaching forward: one for each step of progress.
entries.greek: ἀναβαίνοντα σαυτὸν αἴσθῃ ... τὰς ιεʹ τῶν ἀναβαθμῶν ᾠδάς
entries.evidence: The fifteen Songs of Ascents: every one from Eng 120 to 134 carries the superscription 'A song of ascents'. The copy printed the LXX range (it also does so at §§4 and 17).

entries.situation: When stray thoughts have carried you captive and you notice and repent: stop there, sit down and weep as the people did.
entries.greek: Ἠχμαλωτεύθης ὑπὸ ἀλλοτρίων λογισμῶν ... κάθου, καὶ κλαῦσον ... ρλϛʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 137:1 'By the rivers of Babylon we sat and wept'.

entries.situation: Seeing temptations as a testing of you: to give thanks once they are past.
entries.greek: Τοὺς δὲ πειρασμοὺς ἡγούμενος εἶναί σου δοκιμὴν ... ρληʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 139:1, 23 'You have searched me... test me'.

entries.situation: When enemies hem you in again and you want to be rescued.
entries.greek: Συνέχῃ πάλιν ἀπὸ ἐχθρῶν, καὶ ῥυσθῆναι θέλεις; ... ρλθʹ
entries.evidence: Content: 140:1 'Rescue me, O LORD, from evil men'.

entries.situation: When you want to make petition and pray.
entries.greek: Δεηθῆναι δὲ καὶ προσεύξασθαι θέλεις; ψάλλε τὸν εʹ καὶ ρμβʹ
entries.evidence: The Greek (TLG) and EPE both give only 5 and 142. 143:1 'O LORD, hear my prayer'. The C.S.M.V.'s 140-142 and 145 (LXX) are not in these texts.

entries.situation: When a tyrant enemy rises against the people and you, as Goliath did against David: do not cower but trust as David did.
entries.greek: ὥσπερ Γολιὰθ τῷ Δαβὶδ ... ρμγʹ
entries.evidence: The LXX superscription of 143 reads 'of David, against Goliath'. 144:1 'Who trains my hands for war'.

entries.situation: Marvelling at God's kindness to everyone and remembering His goodness to you, and wanting to bless Him for it.
entries.greek: θαυμάζων τὰς εἰς πάντας τοῦ Θεοῦ εὐεργεσίας ... ἐν τῷ ρμδʹ ψαλμῷ
entries.evidence: The Greek reads ρμδʹ (144), and the EPE translation agrees. Content: 145:9 'The LORD is good to all'. The C.S.M.V. printed 104, hence the copy's 105.

entries.situation: When you want to sing to the Lord.
entries.greek: Ἆσαι θέλεις τῷ Κυρίῳ; ... τὸν ϙβʹ καὶ ϙζʹ
entries.evidence: The Greek (TLG) and EPE both read 92 and 97. The C.S.M.V. read 95 and 97. Eng 96 ('Sing to the LORD a new song') would fit the wording better, so this may be a numeral corruption, but both Greek witnesses say 92.

entries.situation: If you are small yet chosen for some office over your brothers: do not lord it over them, but give glory to the Lord Who chose you.
entries.greek: μικρὸς ὢν προκριθῇς εἰς ἀρχήν ... ρναʹ ἴδιον ὄντα τοῦ Δαβίδ
entries.english: none (LXX 151; not in Protestant or Catholic Bibles; in Orthodox Bibles)
entries.evidence: LXX Psalm 151: 'I was small among my brothers', David chosen and anointed, then fighting Goliath. The BSB has no Psalm 151.

entries.situation: Psalms to sing with the people's refrain 'Alleluia'.
entries.greek: ἐπακοὴν ἔχοντας τὸ Ἀλληλούϊα ... ρδʹ, ρεʹ, ρϛʹ, ριαʹ-ριηʹ, ρλδʹ, ρλεʹ, ρμεʹ-ρνʹ
entries.evidence: Greek list (EPE agrees). LXX 111-118 = Eng 112-119, so the copy wrongly starts at 111 and drops 119.

entries.situation: Psalms about the Saviour: His true begetting from the Father and His coming in the flesh.
entries.greek: τὸν μδʹ καὶ τὸν ρθʹ ... γνησίαν γέννησιν
entries.evidence: Greek numerals. 45:6-7; 110:1, 3.

entries.situation: Foretelling the cross, the plots He endured and how much He suffered for us.
entries.greek: τὸν δὲ καʹ καὶ ξηʹ ... περὶ τοῦ θείου σταυροῦ
entries.evidence: 22:16-18 pierced hands, lots cast; 69:21 gall and vinegar.

entries.situation: Showing the plotting and malice of the Jews and the betrayal by Judas Iscariot.
entries.greek: τὸν μὲν βʹ καὶ ρηʹ ... τὴν Ἰούδα τοῦ Ἰσκαριώτου προδοσίαν
entries.evidence: The Greek reads βʹ (2), and the EPE translation agrees. §15 also pairs Ps 2 with the plot. 109:8 'may another take his office' (Acts 1:20). The C.S.M.V. printed 3.

entries.situation: Showing His kingship and power as Judge, His coming again in the flesh, and the call of the nations.
entries.greek: τόν τε κʹ, καὶ μθʹ, καὶ οαʹ ... κριτικὴν δύναμιν ... τὴν κλῆσιν τῶν ἐθνῶν
entries.evidence: Greek numerals. 50:3-6; 72:1-2, 11.

entries.situation: Showing His resurrection from the dead.
entries.greek: ὁ μὲν ιεʹ δείκνυσιν αὐτοῦ τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀνάστασιν
entries.evidence: 16:10 'You will not let Your Holy One see decay' (Acts 2:27).

entries.situation: Announcing His ascension into heaven.
entries.greek: ὁ δὲ κγʹ καὶ μϛʹ ... τὴν εἰς οὐρανοὺς ἄνοδον
entries.evidence: 24:7-10 'Lift up your heads, O gates'; 47:5 'God has ascended amid shouts of joy'.

entries.situation: Reading these, you can see the benefits the Saviour won for us through His sufferings.
entries.greek: τὸν δὲ ϙβʹ, καὶ ϙεʹ, καὶ ϙζʹ, καὶ ϙηʹ ... διὰ τῶν παθημάτων
entries.evidence: Greek numerals are explicit.

entries.situation: Sadness is soothed when we sing asking our soul why it is so downcast.
entries.greek: τὸ δὲ λυποῦν θεραπεύεται ... Ἵνα τί περίλυπος εἶ, ἡ ψυχή μου
entries.csmv: none printed (the words are quoted without a number)
entries.evidence: The quotation is verbatim LXX 41:6/12 and 42:5, the refrain of Eng 42-43. BSB: 'Why are you downcast, O my soul?'. No number is printed, so there is nothing to be wrong; I marked it false only because no number is given.

entries.situation: A fall or failure is owned when we sing that our feet had nearly slipped.
entries.greek: τὸ μὲν ἐσφαλμένον ἐπιγνώσεται ... Ἐμοῦ δὲ παρὰ μικρὸν ἐσαλεύθησαν οἱ πόδες
entries.csmv: none printed (the words are quoted without a number)
entries.evidence: Verbatim LXX 72:2. BSB 73:2 'my feet had almost stumbled'. The whole psalm is the one Athanasius also gives (§21) for envying the prosperous wicked.

entries.situation: Fear is strengthened by hope when we sing that the Lord is our helper and no man can harm us.
entries.greek: τὸ δὲ φοβηθὲν ἐπιῤῥώσει τῇ ἐλπίδι ... Κύριος ἐμοὶ βοηθὸς, καὶ οὐ φοβηθήσομαι τί ποιήσει μοι ἄνθρωπος
entries.csmv: none printed (the words are quoted without a number)
entries.evidence: Verbatim LXX 117:6 (quoted also in Hebrews 13:6). Eng 56:4, 11 is similar but lacks 'helper'. BSB 118:6 'The LORD is on my side; I will not be afraid'.

entries.situation: The Psalmist's own example of meditating on God's words; whoever cares for sufferers should use Scripture's words.
entries.greek: ἔλεγεν ἐν τῷ ριηʹ ψαλμῷ· Ἐν τοῖς δικαιώμασί σου μελετήσω ... Ψαλτὰ ἦσάν μοι ... Εἰ μὴ ὅτι ὁ νόμος σου μελέτη μου
entries.evidence: Greek ριηʹ = 118. 119:92 'If Your law had not been my delight, I would have perished in my affliction'.

entries.situation: (Content, not use) Creation, as told in Genesis, is sung in these.
entries.greek: τὰ μὲν γὰρ τῆς Γενέσεως ψάλλει ἐν τῷ ὀκτωκαιδεκάτῳ ... καὶ ἐν τῷ κγʹ
entries.evidence: Greek numbers are spelled out. 19:1; 24:1-2.

entries.situation: (Content) The exodus from Egypt, the plagues and the tabernacle.
entries.greek: ἐν τῷ ἑβδομηκοστῷ ἑβδόμῳ ... ἑκατοστῷ τρισκαιδεκάτῳ; ἑκατοστῷ τετάρτῳ; ἑκατὸν πέμπτον; ἐξοδίῳ σκηνῆς ἐν τῷ κηʹ
entries.evidence: The Greek names only two exodus psalms; the copy's added 106 is not in the Greek. 105 and 29 are correct. The LXX title of 28 reads 'at the going out of the tabernacle'.

entries.situation: (Content) The time of Joshua and the Judges: they built cities and planted, and they cried to the Lord in trouble and He saved them.
entries.greek: Τὰ δὲ τοῦ Ναυῆ καὶ τῶν Κριτῶν ... ἐν τῷ ἑκατοστῷ ἕκτῳ ... ἐκέκραξαν πρὸς Κύριον ἐν τῷ θλίβεσθαι
entries.evidence: Greek 'hundred and sixth' = LXX 106. Content: 107:36-37 settle cities, sow fields and plant vineyards; 107:6 'they cried out to the LORD in their trouble'. Eng 105 has neither.

entries.situation: (Content) The kings, and the return from exile told in Ezra.
entries.greek: τὰ τῶν Βασιλειῶν ... ἐν τῷ ἐννεακαιδεκάτῳ; τὰ δὲ τοῦ Ἔσδρα ἐν τῷ ἑκατονεικοστῷ πέμπτῳ ... ἑκατονεικοστῷ πρώτῳ
entries.evidence: 20:7 chariots and horses; 126:1; 122:1. Only the bracketed Gradual range is wrong (it should read 120-134).

entries.situation: (Prophecy) The Saviour's coming and His being the Father's Word.

problems: Printed-number errors in the English copy (scratchpad marcellinus.txt), with the Greek-verified English numbers. §4 Joshua/Judges, 'They cried unto the Lord': the copy says 105, it is 107. §3 exodus: the copy adds 106, which is not in the Greek. The Gradual Psalms are printed '119-133' three times; they are 120-134. §12 faith and prayer: the copy has 11 and 12; the Greek (TLG) has Eng 12 and 17 (disputed). §14: 'hortatory 32' should be 33; 'confessions, notably the 51st' misrepresents the Greek. §16 vintage: 19 should be 84. §16 'as though God had forgotten you': 27 should be 13. §17 prayer against enemies: 140 should be 141. §21 thankful-acknowledgement list: 71 and 126 should be dropped. §22 anger abated and captivity ended: 116 should be 126. §23 Monday: 95 should be 48. §24 how to praise: drop 113, 117 and 149. §25 prayer and supplication: '5, 141-143, 146' should be '5, 143'. §25 God's kindness to all: 105 should be 145. §25 'sing to Him': '96, 98' should be '93, 98' by the Greek. §25 Alleluia list: '111-118' should be '112-119'. §26 plot of the Jews and Judas: 3 should be 2.
The English copy OMITS a pairing entirely: the Sabbath (Saturday) psalm, Greek ϙαʹ = LXX 91 = Eng 92 ('A song for the Sabbath day'), in the Greek and in the EPE translation.

The copy's errors have two sources. (a) The C.S.M.V. translation itself misreads some numerals: its Septuagint-numbered text at fisheaters.com has 18 for 83, 26 for 12, 94 for 47, 104 for 144, 114-115 for 125, 139 for 140, and 3 for 2. (b) The later conversion to English numbering is inconsistent: the Gradual range was left unconverted, 'Psalm 104' was left as 105 in §4, and 118 was added in §21. Any number taken from the copy must be checked against the Greek.

Readings within the Greek that are uncertain. The TLG/Migne text reads ιϛʹ (16) for 'saved from your enemies' and πϛʹ (86) in the §17 prayer list. EPE and the C.S.M.V. both read 17 and 87. Content (the superscription of Eng 18; the prayer in Eng 88) favours 17 and 87, and I followed them. §12 'trust and prayer' is ιαʹ, ιϛʹ (11, 16) in the TLG but 10, 11 in the C.S.M.V.; I left it at low confidence. §25 'sing to the Lord' is ϙβʹ (92) in both the TLG and EPE, although Eng 96 opens 'Sing to the LORD'.

Extraction caveat: in the Documenta Catholica Omnia PDF, stigma (6) and koppa (90) drop onto separate lines. I rejoined them by position. The one numeral lost is in the §14 praise list and does not affect any §§15-26 pairing.

Septuagint splits and merges that the site must cite by verse. LXX 9 = Eng 9-10. LXX 113 = Eng 114-115. LXX 114 = Eng 116:1-9 (thanks when heard, §15). LXX 115 = Eng 116:10-19 (faith in prayer, §24). LXX 146/147 = Eng 147:1-11 and 147:12-20. LXX 151 (authority, §25) has no English-Bible equivalent: it is in Orthodox Bibles only, so a quiz result using it needs a note, or it should be left out.

The C.S.M.V. heavily abridges §14 (the genre classification). The Greek lists about twenty categories with many more psalms. It also renders ἐξομολόγησις as 'confession' there and in §21 ('testify'). In both places the Greek word means thankful acknowledgement of God; the listed psalms are the ones that open 'I will give thanks' or 'Give thanks'. Psalm 51 is not among them. Do not present §21's list as psalms for confessing sin.

Not consulted: Gregg's 1980 Paulist translation (no online text found), the Savvidis-Wyrwa critical edition (De Gruyter), and Scribd's 'Psalms for Various Occasions' (login). The critical edition could settle the four uncertain numerals above.

Minor slips in the copy: '1 Kings 23:13ff' for the Ziphites means 1 Kingdoms = 1 Samuel 23. The fisheaters mirror prints 'Psalm 150' for David's own psalm where the Greek has ρναʹ (151). The closing lines (sadness, failure, fear) print no numbers; they are Eng 42:5/42:11/43:5, 73:2 and 118:6, all verbatim LXX in the Greek.
Section numbers for §§15-26 follow the Greek section markers in the EPE translation (ιε΄ to κς΄). §12, §14, §§3-8, §29 and §33 are estimates of the conventional 33-section division.
